messages:
Maya: quick ping — saw a weird perf regression on the continuous-batcher morning run, looks correlated with kernel fallback churn and KV cache misses.
Alex: summary? p95 up, throughput down?
Maya: p95 decode latency +35% on a subset of traffic (mostly 50–400 token prompts). throughput dropped ~12% on the small-prompt cohort. tracer shows a spike in kernel-selection time and KV cache eviction churn.
Sam: do you have the profiler traces?
Maya: pasted snippet below (trimmed):
```
# decode timeline sample
kernel_select: 18.2ms -> fallback_quantized: 14.9ms -> launch_wait: 3.1ms
kv_cache_evict: 7.4ms (burst) ; kv_prefetch_miss: 0.9ms x 6
batch_form_time median: 6.2ms -> 12.8ms during spike
```

Jin: hmm looks like when we hit a particular decode-rate + length combo the runtime flips kernel strategy and prefetch budget collapses, causing eviction thrash. is this the same window where admission started making larger micro-batches?
Maya: yes — admission allowed microbatch size to grow for decode-rate < 60 tok/s but those requests still have short prefixes, so KV cache locality is low. batcher then combines very heterogeneous sequences and kernel selector toggles to a heavier path.
Nitin: can we adjust token-budget target per workload class rather than a global threshold? i.e. keep small-prompt class token_budget=40, medium=120, long=400. also maybe cap microbatch growth when kv_prefetch_miss rate > 3/min.
Alex: +1, but need to avoid regressions for long-form. propose classifier on arrival: length_bucket + observed decode-rate -> pick admission policy + kernel hint.
Sam: I ran a quick reclassifier in staging: split by prompt_len < 128, 128-512, >512 and decode_rate buckets (<60, 60-300, >300). tuned token_budget targets and disabled late kernel fallback for small bucket. Deploy logs:
```
# config snippet
continuous_batching.classifier = "promptstride"
promptstride.buckets = ["<128","128-512",">512"]
promptstride.decode_rate = [60,300]
admission.token_budget = {"<128":40, "128-512":120, ">512":400}
kernel.hint.disable_fallback = {"<128": true}
kv.prefetch.threshold = 3
```
deploy-bot: deploy starting: ci/build/3145 -> staging (sam/experiment-ps)

Sam: quick results from 30m A/B: small-bucket p95 decode latency down 25% (240ms -> 180ms), microbatch size median unchanged, kv_prefetch_miss rate down 60%. overall token cost -7% on the traffic slice.
Maya: nice. did we see any long-form regressions?
Sam: long bucket stable, slight throughput increase (2%). medium bucket unchanged. no error spike.
Jin: did kernel-selector logs show fewer fallbacks?
Sam: yes — we removed the policy that coerced fallback when batch variance > 0.65 for small prompts; kernel_select path stayed on fast-quantized path more often. fallback_count down 78% for small bucket.
Nitin: sounds promising, need a 24h run and canary rollout plan. also add metric: kv_cache_locality_ratio per bucket + alert on >10% sudden drop.
Alex: agree. next steps: (1) prod canary at 2% traffic with classifier and token budgets; (2) add metric and alert; (3) keep kernel.hint.disable_fallback for small bucket for now. Sam can own rollout.
Maya: I'll attach profiler traces and a short writeup for the oncall runbook (how to revert token budgets & classifier).
Sam: starting canary tomorrow 07:00 UTC. will paste dashboards.
Nitin: thanks, team.
Maya: thx :thumbsup:
